```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Use `oauth_db_oracle()` to query Oracle Database with each visitor's
Microsoft Entra account. It returns a DBI connection for SQL and dbplyr.
Oracle maps the visitor to a database schema and applies their database
privileges. The database can run on your infrastructure or in the cloud,
including Oracle Autonomous Database, if it supports Entra integration.

## Set up the database and driver

Ask your database administrator for an Oracle service configured for
[Microsoft Entra authentication](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/26/dbseg/configuring-oracle-database-microsoft-entra-id-integration.html),
a TCPS listener address and port, and the database's Entra Application ID
URI. Your users must have the corresponding global-schema or app-role
mapping in Oracle. Signing in to the Shiny app does not create that mapping.

Install the R package `odbc` and Oracle Instant Client's **Basic** and
**ODBC** packages for the architecture of your R process. Register the
Oracle ODBC driver and find its name with `odbc::odbcListDrivers()`.
Use a current supported Oracle client with Entra token support. Oracle
documents support for the 19c thick client from 19.16 and for newer
supported releases; the 21c thick client does not support this integration.
Check both your database and client versions against Oracle's
[ODBC setup guide](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/26/odbcd/using-oracle-database-odbc-driver.html)
and [client support table](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/26/dbseg/supported-client-drivers-entra-ad-connections.html).

The client needs a trusted TLS certificate chain. Depending on the client,
platform and database, use its configured trust store or pass an Oracle
wallet directory as `wallet_location`. A database requiring mutual TLS
also needs the client certificate in that wallet. Use `server_cert_dn`
when your administrator supplies the expected certificate distinguished
name; otherwise the client matches the hostname. Certificate matching
is always enabled.

## Register the Shiny application

Register a Microsoft Entra **Web** application with redirect URI
`http://localhost:8100`. Add the delegated permission exposed by your
database's Entra registration, commonly `session:scope:connect`, and
obtain the required consent. This is a separate registration from the
database server registration. See Oracle's
[registration example](https://docs.oracle.com/en/learn/ocidb-auth-msentraid/)
and [Microsoft app registration](oauth-setup.html#register-a-microsoft-entra-app).

Your administrator must configure the database registration's access-token
claims and Oracle user mappings. For Entra v2 access tokens, Oracle's
setup includes the `upn` access-token claim. Request the database's own
resource and scope; an Azure SQL access token has a different audience.

Save the app settings in your local `.Renviron` and restart R:

```text
OAUTHDB_TENANT_ID=your-tenant-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-shiny-app-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-shiny-app-client-secret
OAUTHDB_ORACLE_RESOURCE=api://your-database-application-id
OAUTHDB_ORACLE_HOST=database.example.org
OAUTHDB_ORACLE_SERVICE=reporting.example.org
OAUTHDB_ORACLE_DRIVER=Oracle in instantclient_19_30
```

| Setting | Where to find it |
| --- | --- |
| `OAUTHDB_ORACLE_RESOURCE` | Database server's Entra Application ID URI, not the Shiny application's client ID |
| Delegated scope | Database registration's **Expose an API** page; replace `session:scope:connect` below if needed |
| Host, service and TCPS port | Oracle connection details supplied by the administrator |
| Driver | Installed driver name reported by `odbc::odbcListDrivers()` |
| Wallet and certificate DN, if needed | Oracle administrator's TLS configuration |

## A complete app

The Microsoft client accepts custom token targets. Oracle has a
deployment-specific resource, so configure an `oracle` target explicitly:

```{r app}
library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

resource <- Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_ORACLE_RESOURCE")
scope <- paste0(resource, "/session:scope:connect")
client <- oauth_db_microsoft_client(
  tenant_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_TENANT_ID"),
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100",
  token_targets = list(
    oracle = list(
      resource = resource,
      scopes = scope,
      required_scopes = scope
    )
  )
)

ui <- oauth_ui(
  fluidPage(
    actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
    actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
    tableOutput("rows")
  ),
  id = "auth",
  client = client
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client, auto_redirect = FALSE)
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  con <- oauth_db_oracle(
    auth$connection,
    host = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_ORACLE_HOST"),
    service_name = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_ORACLE_SERVICE"),
    driver = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_ORACLE_DRIVER"),
    port = 1522L,
    target = "oracle"
  )
  output$rows <- renderTable({
    connection <- con()
    DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT USER AS database_user FROM DUAL")
  })
}

runApp(
  shinyApp(ui, server, uiPattern = ".*"),
  port = 8100,
  launch.browser = FALSE
)
```

Save the code as `example.R`, set your TCPS port and any wallet or
certificate DN arguments, then run `source("example.R")`. Open
`http://localhost:8100` in your regular browser and sign in. The example
shows the Oracle session user. Replace the query with a table or view
the user can read.

## Connections and token files

shinyOAuth handles browser sign-in and token renewal. The adapter obtains
the current access token when opening a connection. It supplies a separate
Oracle Net descriptor containing `TOKEN_AUTH=OAUTH` and the location of a
temporary token file. It does not change shared Oracle configuration files
or the process's `TNS_ADMIN` environment variable.

The token file is removed after connection opening, including on error
or interrupt. On Unix, its directory is private (`0700`) and the file has
mode `0600`. On Windows, use a private R temporary directory because
access rules are inherited from its parent directory.

Before returning a connection, the helper queries
`SYS_CONTEXT('USERENV', 'AUTHENTICATION_METHOD')` and requires Oracle's
`TOKEN_GLOBAL` result. A different method or a failed check closes the
connection. The helper disables network authentication alternatives and
Oracle ODBC automatic failover. Reopen a broken connection by calling
`con()` so the new connection gets a current token.

A valid database session survives ordinary token renewal. Account changes,
permission loss, sign-out and Shiny session end close it. Always call
`con()` before querying; a previously retained native handle is not a new
authorization check. Oracle still decides which database objects and rows
the visitor may access.

This helper supports Oracle's Entra OAuth bearer-token path. It does not
implement OCI IAM proof-of-possession authentication, password login,
proxy-user connections or arbitrary OIDC issuers. There is no local
Oracle/Entra Docker demo. The automated tests check the ODBC boundary,
credential cleanup, token-authentication verification and Shiny lifecycle;
they do not establish a live Oracle/Entra connection.
